scope: Current V2 limitations and decisions. Retired Pre-Alpha assessment and numerical experiments live in Git history, not the runtime distribution.

findings.disposition: Advanced Fluids V2 has operator gameplay/visual acceptance on Experimental. Alpha compiled lock remains; this purge does not unlock or publish it.

Hidden Game rendering and editing-preview LOD were corrected. Current whole-frame SDK editor/standalone observations are recorded in docs/WHOLE_ENGINE_PERFORMANCE.md; different viewport sizes and workloads do not establish universal editor/runtime parity.
Humanoid get-up and animation blending remain limited; no claim of general natural physical recovery.
Linux qualification is current per purge evidence. Earlier Windows/Android hardware acceptance does not certify this changed checkpoint.

Portable rendering and CPU particle simulation/collision remain legitimate capability fallbacks, not historical compatibility. The whole-engine audit qualifies a real 5,000-particle CPU fallback separately from unsupported required-GPU authoring.
Content-dependent dense contact and CCD safety limits remain; removal of MK1 diagnostics does not change MK2 algorithms.
The operator accepted the architectural purge before the Vehicles/Wheels V2 milestone. This records that decision; it does not promote main or publish a V2 release.

One local NVIDIA terrain depth capture and one first-dispatch one-slot particle test failed in the purge full run; unchanged isolated reruns passed. Cause remains unestablished. Assertions and GPU algorithms remain unchanged; see purge qualification evidence.
The current mod format does not admit native Terrain V2 assets; ordinary cooked mesh/scene mods and base-game terrain remain. Retired M75 fork/cook workflows are not retained.

Whole-engine audit improved ordinary gameplay without changing accepted physical outcomes. Severe CCD impacts, IK tails and queue-inclusive completion still miss defined 120/60 FPS or 5 ms goals; see docs/WHOLE_ENGINE_PERFORMANCE.md. Functional or relative p99 passes are not universal performance qualification.

The local four-model yard retains about 3.12 GiB process RSS plus swap, including decoded images needed for resource recreation. Active pinned assets exceed the cache target. This is a footprint follow-up, not proof of unbounded growth; private models remain outside Git and SDKs.
